advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide/document whether legacy-Jira inference should also apply on the SNAPSHOT restore path, or explicitly note that already-compacted pre-feature Jira tickets stay 'unknown'.
evidence: src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:199: `if data.get("creation_channel") is None:` then `_project_legacy_creation_channel(state)` — only reached from process_create
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:806: `for key, value in compiled_state.items(): state[key] = value` in process_snapshot restores creation_channel verbatim with no legacy-Jira reprojection
src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py:181 comment: 're-seeds from its compacted_at (replay discards the pre-snapshot events)' — the genesis envelope needed for inference is gone after compaction
Docstring at _processors.py:232-234 acknowledges 'the SNAPSHOT-fold path a later story adds reuses this exact state-shaped interface' — confirming the snapshot path is intentionally NOT wired up yet
advisory.finding: The legacy-Jira inference runs only on the raw-event process_create path, not on the SNAPSHOT restore path. A legacy Jira ticket compacted before this feature has creation_channel='unknown' persisted in its snapshot compiled_state and process_snapshot restores it verbatim, so it never upgrades to 'jira' — the same logical ticket projects 'jira' if uncompacted but 'unknown' if compacted.
scenarios: A pre-feature Jira ticket that has already been compacted into a SNAPSHOT is queried after this change — it stays 'unknown' while an equivalent uncompacted ticket infers 'jira'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document that legacy-Jira inference only backfills tickets written under the default 'reconciler' author/env_id (deployments with custom REBAR_AUTHOR/REBAR_ENV_ID are not covered).
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:173-174: `_rebar_env("ENV_ID", LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID)` / `_rebar_env("AUTHOR", LEGACY_JIRA_AUTHOR)` — REBAR_* overrides win over the default, so historical events may carry a non-'reconciler' identity
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:240-241: `state.get("author") == LEGACY_JIRA_AUTHOR and state.get("env_id") == LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID` — inference matches only the literal 'reconciler'
advisory.finding: The inbound-Jira recorded path and the legacy inference both key on author/env_id == 'reconciler'. When REBAR_AUTHOR/REBAR_ENV_ID are set to non-default values in production (a supported override in _event_meta), pre-feature Jira CREATEs written under those custom identities will not match the legacy signature and stay 'unknown', so the backfill silently covers only deployments that ran with the reconciler defaults.
scenarios: A deployment that set REBAR_AUTHOR/REBAR_ENV_ID before this feature shipped: its legacy Jira tickets never infer 'jira'.
